Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.rt

Class StandardLibrary

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.rt.StandardLibrary
All Implemented Interfaces:
Builtins
public final class StandardLibrary extends Object implements Builtins
The vocabulary every Mandela host shares: the methods on the built-in types, the global functions, and the std.* modules.

The interpreter deliberately knows nothing about join, upper or sqrt. It asks this class, through Builtins, whenever a member is not a declared field or method, and a host is free to answer differently: a Web Browser page installs a library whose fs module has no grants, an Espresso panel one whose println goes to its Problems view. What lives here is the desktop-shaped default.

Three kinds of name

  • properties — s.length, m.keys. Read as values, never called. Cheap, because every member read that misses a declared field walks this table.
  • methods — l.map(f). Resolved to a callable that already knows its receiver, so the machine only has to pass the arguments.
  • modules — use std.json installs one map under the short name, so a script writes json.parse(text) and the group stays discoverable without polluting the global table.

Failures

Everything thrown here is a MandelaError, so script code can catch it with try / catch and the kind name is stable: TypeError for a value of the wrong shape, ValueError for a bad argument or a missing name, PermissionError for a refused capability, IOError for the filesystem. A Java exception escaping a library function would leave the script with nothing to match on.

Callback-taking methods (map, filter, sort) re-enter the machine through Machine.invoke(org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.values.Callable, java.lang.Object, java.lang.Object[]), which is the barrier path described on VM: a script callback may itself call map, and the nesting is bounded by the sandbox's depth budget.

  • Method Details

    • member

      public Object member(Machine machine, Object receiver, String name)
      Resolves a member on a value that has no declared members of its own.

      Implementations must be cheap: this runs on the member-access path of every "list".join(", ")-style expression. The returned callable already knows its receiver, so the machine just calls it with the arguments the call site gave.

      The running Machine is handed over rather than stored: a library function that calls a script callback (map, sort with a comparator, a widget's handler) has to re-enter the machine that is executing it, and one library table is shared by every machine a host creates.

      A map answers its own keys first, which is what makes a module object (json.parse) and any record-shaped value read naturally; only a missing key falls through to the methods a map has of its own.

      Specified by:
      member in interface Builtins
      Parameters:
      machine - the interpreter that is running this expression
      receiver - the value whose member is being read
      name - the member name
      Returns:
      a value, or a Callable to call, or null when there is none

    • globals

      public MandelaMap globals(Machine machine)
      Publishes the global functions a script may call without a use.

      Kept small on purpose: println and the conversions are the whole set, because every name here competes with a script's own declaration and with a host's own bindings.

      The console functions close over the machine they are installed in, which is what routes a page script's println to the browser console and an Espresso panel's to its Problems view — never to System.out.

      Parameters:
      machine - the interpreter these names will run on
      Returns:
      the names and their values, for a global table

    • install

      public void install(Machine machine, Map<String,Object> globals, Map<String,Object> own)
      Installs the library's globals and this machine's own bindings into a global table, the one call a host makes to wire a fresh VM up.

      The two hooks the compiler looks for by name go in here as well, because they are what makes use and import work at all: a use statement compiles to a call on __use__, which asks this library for the module on the running machine. Passing null own still installs them, so a host that does nothing else gets a language that behaves the same as everyone else's.

      Parameters:
      machine - the interpreter about to run
      globals - the live global table
      own - the host's functions, installed last so a host may replace a name the library offers

    • valueMemberNames

      public List<String> valueMemberNames(String typeName)
      The members one built-in type answers to, for a tool that lists them.

      This is the same table member(org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.vm.Machine, java.lang.Object, java.lang.String) resolves against, enumerated rather than called, so an editor's completion popup cannot run a library function or need a capability to fill itself. The order is the resolution order too: properties before methods, because a property read shadows a method of the same name.

      A Bool carries no members and an unknown type name answers empty rather than guessing: typeOf is the authority on what a value is, and a name invented here would be offered to the developer and then fail at runtime.

      Parameters:
      typeName - Str, List, Map, Range, or a number under any of the names the language uses for one
      Returns:
      the member names, empty when the type has none
